description: Dalaran Heist bosses E and the Heist finale (phase 8 family 18): twelve encounters of The Dalaran Heist (Sael'orn, Haro Setting-Sun, Dagg Cruelmight, Banker Biggs, Valdera Highborne, Marei Loom, Lilayell Suntear, Sky Captain Smiggs, Anarii Duskgrove, Kazamon Steelskin, Hesutu Stonewind, Kara Stamper) and the four fixed bosses of the Heist finale (Magistrix Norroa, Archmage Vargoth, Archmage Kalec, Archmage Khadgar; Twist - The Finale, DALA_830, is the rule of the schedule's finale block), with the boss card Kirin Tor Elemental. Commander Bolan is rejected (data gap). Boss deck lists are transcribed from hearthstone.wiki.gg boss pages (read 2026-11-14), by card name; tools/dungeon-run-catalog (step 'encounters') resolves the names against facts/violet-hold-2026-09.json, checks every card and writes data/dungeon-run/encounters-v1.json. Level: the Heist boss pages have no level table. The deck grows with the boss's level (10 cards at level 1, 15 at 2, 20 at 3, 25 at 4 and 5, 30 from 6: the notes of Whirt the All-Knowing, Albin Eastoft and Awilo, the rule of families 14 and 15), so a quantity table of 30 cards ("These decks correspond only to level 6" where the page says so) is level 6, a pool table's 'Total cards' gives the sizes at the boss's levels and the row takes the lowest level that holds the largest, and a hero printed with 10 Health is a level-1 boss; a chapter's final boss is tier 4. Tier: levels 1-2: tier 1; 3-4: tier 2; 5-6: tier 3; 7-8: tier 4 (the encounter model's level table); the fight's Health is the act curve's, not the printed 30 or 10.
method: Each page's wikitext (?action=raw) was read and its deck table transcribed by the family 14 table reader: rowspan- and colspan-aware, column by column in table order, Normal and Heroic separately. A 'Possible cards' pool lists each card once; a 'Quantity' table keeps its counts. The wiki's link target is the card name; the boss-only card carries its id. Generated by verify/tools/gen/p8f18/make_f18.py.

Web Grab (0), "Your opponent summons a minion from their hand": Dirty Rat's pull (CFM_790's rule): one random minion of the run player's hand (the game RNG) is summoned to that player's board, without its Battlecry; nothing when that hand holds no minion or that board is full. The summoned minion becomes public as any summon does; the rest of the hand stays hidden. It is offered while the run player's board has room and hand holds a card (both public); in the boss's fair view the hidden cards are no minions, so its search pulls nothing (the real pull is a random public event).

Phase Spider (DALA_BOSS_61t) is not in either of the wiki's deck lists: the wiki calls it "an unused card intended for use during Sael'orn encounter" and lists its voice lines under Unused, so the row has no Phase Spider (family 18 records the card as rejected: unused in the adventure).

Next... (0), "Swap the left-most card in each player's hand with one in their deck": for each player whose hand and deck both hold a card, the left-most hand card is shuffled into that player's deck (its hand enchantments are lost, as a card returned to a deck loses them) and a random card of that deck (the game RNG, picked before the shuffle) takes the left-most hand slot. Each player sees the card that came to the own hand; what the opponent believed about either player's hand and deck is reset (RunHelpers.BeliefReset), so the boss never learns the run player's new card. Offered while either player has a card in hand and in deck (zone counts, public).

Steelskin: "You can't damage yourself": damage that a source of the boss deals to the boss's own hero is prevented (no damage, no Armor lost, no damage event; Actions.EncounterRules.PreventsSelfDamage, read by Character.TakeDamage before the hero's other damage rules), so his deck's self-damage (Hellfire, Kobold Librarian, Chittering Tunneler, Blood Witch, Dread Infernal, Crystallizer's 5 damage while it still gives Armor) costs him nothing. Health lost without damage (a Health cost) is not damage, and Fatigue is the game's rule, not his source: it still hurts. The run player's sources hurt him as usual.

Soul Weave (3), "Discard a card. Summon a random minion of the same cost": one random card of the boss's own hand (the game RNG; the engine's discard) and then one random scripted minion of any class that costs what the discarded card cost in hand, from the pool the run's generation filter allows for the boss; nothing summoned when no minion has that Cost or the board is full. Offered while the boss holds a card and its board has room.

The Heist's finale: Chapter 5, Kirin Tor Citadel, has twelve fights, and the last four are always the same, Magistrix Norroa, Archmage Vargoth, Archmage Kalec and Archmage Khadgar, in that order (the wiki's Dalaran Heist page, Twists: "Four Additional Encounters: (Chapter 5) There are four additional bosses in the fifth chapter, for a total of twelve bosses. The last four bosses are always the same for every run"; Twist - The Finale, DALA_830). Here the four are the fixed bosses of the schedule's finale (tier finale: never drawn by a combat or major slot), at levels 9-12; the fight's Health is the finale's curve. A finale deck keeps the wiki's count (35 cards, Normal column).

Kaironomaly: "Your opponent has 25 seconds to take their turn": at the start of each of the run player's turns that player's turn timer (the client's TIMEOUT tag, which Nozdormu the Eternal sets to 15) is 25 seconds unless it is shorter already (Actions.EncounterRules.KaironomalySeconds). The engine has no clock: the harnesses play the tag; the client's match (NativeMatch) ends a turn whose timer is short, for 15 and 25 alike (EncounterRules.ShortTurnSeconds). The wiki's note (Nozdormu on the board disrupts the power) is the old Nozdormu's aura, not a rule of the boss.

Summon Elemental (3), "Summon a 2/3 Elemental. It copies your spells.": the wiki's special card Kirin Tor Elemental (DALA_504, "Your spells cast an additional time"). After its controller casts a spell, a copy is cast again on the same target (RecastRules.Recast, Pirate's Mark's rule: a target that is gone loses only the targeted part, a Choose One copy keeps the option picked); a copy never casts again, so each Elemental adds one cast; a Secret or a Quest is not cast twice. It needs a free board slot.
Archmage's Apprentice (KARA_00_08, the wiki's "Boss" card, also in Chronomancer Inara's deck) is family 09's script.

rejected.name: Commander Bolan
rejected.reason: A Quest! ("Give your opponent a Quest!") hands the run player one of five quests (DALA_BOSS_75e1 Bear Liver Quest, 75e2 Murloc Quest, 75e3 Turtle Escort Quest, 75e4 Herbalist Quest, 75e5 Hogger Quest) whose completion ends the fight; the client data gives the five enchantments a name and no text, no requirement and no reward tags, and the wiki gives none either (its page: no deck, "will instead summon minions from turn to turn like Tad", "Upon completion of any event, the reward choice is given and the battle ends"; the quest names have no page, only rows marked Unknown in the Rise of Shadows enchantment list), nor the minions he summons. Neither the quests nor the fight can be built from a source
rejected.lift: none: a data gap no phase owns; it needs a source for the five quests' requirements and Bolan's summon list (a transcription of the original encounter), then a script of the quests as run-player enchantments that end the fight with a no-loss win (EncounterRules.EndWithNoLoss)
